title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the continuation of 'La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois', Grothendieck is building an abstract group-theoretic framework (Π-groups) to describe fundamental groups of curves of type (g,ν) in the anabelian setting. The previous page notes that a moduli 'multiplicity' over Q or Z for a given discrete combinatorial type π0 would be fibred in groupoids over a 2-category of schemes rather than an ordinary category, which he flags as a conceptual difficulty.

This page writes down the universal case, the exact sequence (13):
1 → Π̂_{g,ν} → π1(U_{g,ν,Q}) → π1(M_{g,ν,Q}) → 1.
- U_{g,ν,Q} → M_{g,ν,Q} is the universal (open) curve of type (g,ν) over the moduli stack in characteristic 0. U_{g,ν} is essentially M_{g,ν+1}.
- Π̂_{g,ν} is the profinite completion of the surface group of a fibre.
- He names the middle group M_{g,ν} and the right-hand group N_{g,ν}.
This is the arithmetic, profinite Birman exact sequence. Its image in Out(Π̂) is the arithmetic profinite mapping class group, mapping onto G_Q.

He says the middle group π1(U_{g,ν,Q}) 'appears as a profinite Π-group'. He wants to isolate a property common to:
- this universal case, and
- the relative cases of a curve over a base field k finitely generated over Q.
He remarks that the universal case essentially reduces to the second by passing to the generic point of M_{g,ν}: the generic curve is defined over the function field Q(M_{g,ν}), which is finitely generated over Q.

He then starts an axiomatisation. A Π-group M comes with homomorphisms K_i: T → M, where T is a 'torus', i.e. a copy of Ẑ(1). These are given up to conjugacy and form a 'ponctuation' (classes K_i^…) modelling the inertia groups at the ν cusps.

The next page completes the set-up:
- a distinguished normal profinite subgroup Π with extension 1 → Π → M → N → 1;
- a torus K: T ↪ Π with image L;
- the normaliser N(L), whose image of N(L)/L in N is open;
- the action of N(L)/L on L through a cyclotomic character χ_N: N → Ẑ*.
The 'essential hypothesis' then concerns the image of this character (presumably that it is open in Ẑ*).

In modern terms, he is axiomatising 'outer Galois representations of a profinite surface group with cuspidal inertia, compatible with a cyclotomic character'. The aim is to isolate the structure common to all arithmetic families of hyperbolic curves in characteristic 0, as input for anabelian, section-conjecture-type statements.
errors: Notational clash: M_{g,ν} denotes both the moduli multiplicity and the group π1(U_{g,ν,Q}); N_{g,ν} also collides with N(L) on the next page.
Exactness on the left (injectivity of Π̂ → π1(U)) needs hyperbolicity, 2g-2+ν>0, and characteristic 0. This is implicit but standard.

The reduction of the universal case to the generic point is only 'essentially' valid. π1 of the generic point surjects onto π1(M_{g,ν}) but is much larger, so one recovers the universal case as a quotient rather than an equivalence. Grothendieck hedges appropriately.

ideas.what: Profinite arithmetic Birman exact sequence for the universal curve over M_{g,ν,Q}
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy exact sequence for the universal curve / profinite Birman sequence, π1(M_{g,ν+1}) → π1(M_{g,ν})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birman (topological); arithmetic version Ihara, Oda, Nakamura, Matsumoto (1980s-90s)
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (1981) and Esquisse d'un programme discuss π1 of M_{g,ν} acting on Π̂_{g,ν}

ideas.what: Reducing the universal family to the generic curve over the function field of M_{g,ν}
ideas.modern_name: Generic curve; Galois action of the generic point
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; used by Nakamura, Matsumoto, Hoshi–Mochizuki

ideas.what: Abstract 'Π-group' M with a distinguished profinite surface subgroup Π, cuspidal 'tori' K_i: T=Ẑ(1) → M given up to conjugacy, and a cyclotomic character read off from normalisers of inertia
ideas.modern_name: Outer representations of cuspidal type (cf. Hoshi–Mochizuki 'NN-type/IPSC-type' outer representations); group-theoretic characterisation of cuspidal inertia and the cyclotomic character
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura (characterisation of inertia, 1990s); Mochizuki, Hoshi–Mochizuki (combinatorial anabelian geometry, 2000s-2010s)
ideas.where_published: Π-groups appear in La Longue Marche, but this specific axiomatisation in the continuation pages appears unpublished

ideas.what: Moduli of curves with given π0 'type' as a 2-stack (previous page)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets out to axiomatise, group-theoretically and uniformly for the universal family and for curves over finitely generated fields, the data of a profinite surface group, cuspidal inertia 'tori', and the cyclotomic character obtained from normalisers of inertia. This closely anticipates the abstract outer-representation frameworks of Hoshi–Mochizuki's combinatorial anabelian geometry and Nakamura's characterisation of cuspidal inertia. To my knowledge these are not traced back to these unpublished Longue Marche continuation pages.
missed.quote: Je voudrais dégager une propriété commune à ce cas "universel" (13), et aux cas relatifs à un corps de base k extension de type fini de Q
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority and motivation for the abstract 'IPSC/NN-type' frameworks. The full axiom set on later pages may contain conditions not yet considered.

missed.claim: The axiomatic definition of the common property (the 'essential hypothesis' on the image of the cyclotomic character) is begun here and continued on the next pages; whether it is completed and used is unclear from this page.
missed.quote: considérons un Π-groupe M, et un homomorphisme K_i : T → M
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could be compared with the minimal hypotheses needed for the combinatorial section-type and Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type results.

deep.surprise_reason: The exact sequence itself is standard. The interest is in the attempt to axiomatise Π-groups with cuspidal tori and a cyclotomic character across universal and arithmetic cases. This prefigures later abstract frameworks (Nakamura, Hoshi–Mochizuki) and is not widely known, but the page itself contains only the set-up.
transcription_corrections: The middle term of (13) is π1(U_{g,ν,Q}) (the universal curve, same script letter as in the next line), not π1(𝓜_{g,ν,Q}).
'{+et aux cas+} ... {+obtenus [?] relatifs [?]+}' should read: '(13), et aux cas relatifs à un corps de base k extension de type fini de Q'.
The line '(le premier cas se ramenant d'ailleurs essentiellement au second...' contains the word 'essentiellement', taken from the struck-out phrase.
The last line likely begins 'ponctuation : une classe K_i^…' rather than 'important :'. This matches Grothendieck's term for the set of cuspidal inertia classes.
'Ici c'est π1(U_{g,ν,Q}) qui apparaît comme un Π-groupe profini': the '&' is probably a misreading of the subscript bracket.
